recognize_zh: 新生兒周邊血中的中性球細胞質內可見金黃色、具折光性的結晶：A 為數顆菱形／顆粒狀，B 為成束放射狀的針狀結晶，顏色與膽紅素結晶一致，其他白血球與背景紅血球則無此包涵體。
features: Neutrophils containing golden-yellow to orange-brown, refractile intracytoplasmic crystals
Panel A: several small rhomboid/globular crystals scattered among the nuclear lobes
Panel B: sheaf of radiating needle-shaped crystals overlying the neutrophil
Neutrophil nuclei and granules otherwise unremarkable; adjacent lymphocytes lack inclusions
Background red cells with mild anisocytosis, including macrocytes typical of neonatal blood; occasional platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear from a neonate shows neutrophils containing golden-yellow, refractile intracytoplasmic crystals, appearing as small rhomboid granules in one cell and as a sheaf of radiating needles in another. The crystals are non-staining with Wright-Giemsa and retain their intrinsic yellow color, while adjacent lymphocytes and red cells are free of inclusions. Background red cells show neonatal macrocytosis. Findings are consistent with bilirubin crystal inclusions in neutrophils, typically seen in markedly hyperbilirubinemic neonates or as an in vitro artifact of a delayed icteric sample.

ddx.dx: Hemosiderin or malarial pigment in phagocytes
ddx.vs: Hemozoin is brown-black granular and hemosiderin is dark blue-green to brown granular, not bright golden needle-shaped refractile crystals.
Cryoglobulin inclusions are pale blue-gray amorphous or crystalline material that does not have a yellow color.
Stain precipitate is dark purple, lies on top of cells and background alike, and is not confined to neutrophil cytoplasm.
Charcot-Leyden crystals are pale, bipyramidal and associated with eosinophils, not golden needles within neutrophils.
